text: Giddy means so excited that you feel light-headed and silly, like the night before a big trip. Here the man behind the sumo league is giddy because he is sure his idea will be a hit.
Solace is comfort when you feel sad or stressed. Here a boy who kept moving to new cities found solace in football, because the game felt the same everywhere.
Prowess means great skill, usually from lots of practice. Here the wrestlers were picked for their skill at grappling, but also for being fun on camera.
A mawashi is the thick belt-like loincloth that sumo wrestlers wear. Wrestlers also grab each other's mawashi to push and throw. Some American wrestlers are thinking of wearing shorts underneath it.

The dohyo is the raised ring where sumo bouts happen. It is usually made of clay, but this league had a fake one built because it was easier to move. A wrestler loses by stepping out of it or touching the ground with anything but his feet.
A loincloth is a simple piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and between the legs, worn as the only clothing on the lower body.
A veteran is someone who served in the army or another armed force. A combat veteran has actually been in fighting, not just trained for it.
A topknot is hair pulled up and tied into a bundle on the top of the head. Sumo wrestlers in Japan traditionally wear one.
Here strapping is a verb meaning fastening something on with straps or ties. The word can also describe a tall, strong person, as in a strapping young man.
To charge means to rush forward fast. Headfirst means with your head leading the way. In sumo, wrestlers crash into each other's chests right at the start.
This is the coach's slangy way of telling a beginner where to aim her hands: at the upper chest and the armpits, which is how sumo wrestlers push an opponent.
Here electric does not mean powered by electricity. It describes something so thrilling that it makes you tingle with excitement.
A connotation is the feeling that comes along with a word or idea, beyond its plain meaning. A negative connotation means people tend to think of it in a bad or silly way.
Diapers are the soft padded underwear that babies wear. The coach is complaining that people wrongly think sumo wrestlers just look like big babies in diapers.
A debut is the first time someone or something appears in public, like a first game or a first concert.
In a round-robin tournament, every player plays every other player, and the one with the most wins is champion. Nobody is knocked out by one loss.
A bout is one match or contest, especially in boxing, wrestling or sumo.
Here crowned does not mean a real crown was put on a head. It means someone was officially named the champion.
Grappling means fighting by gripping and holding an opponent, as wrestlers do, instead of punching or kicking.
These three words describe a cheerful, lively person who makes others feel good. The league wanted wrestlers who would be fun in interviews.
Here to nail something is a slang way of saying to do it perfectly. It has nothing to do with a hammer.
A chief operating officer, or COO, is a top boss who runs the daily work of a company. It is usually the second-most powerful job after the head boss.
Theatrical means like a play or a show: dramatic and put on for an audience. In pro wrestling, the fights are acted out rather than real contests.
A smackdown is a slangy word for a big, rough fight, and it is also the name of a famous pro-wrestling show.
Cornhole is a lawn game where players toss small beanbags onto a slanted board with a hole in it. It is popular at picnics and tailgates.
When a video or idea goes viral, it spreads very fast as people share it with friends, the way a virus spreads from person to person.
The fringe is the outer edge of something. A fringe sport is one that is outside the mainstream, with only a small group of fans.
A surfer who catches a wave rides it. Here it means that the sport will take off and ride a rush of popularity.
Here to hook someone means to get them so interested that they keep coming back, like catching a fish on a hook.
Something rooted in a thing grows from it, the way a plant grows from its roots. Sumo is rooted in old Japanese traditions.
A commune is a community where people live together and share the work, food and belongings.
Hare Krishna is a name for a Hindu religious movement. Its followers often live in communities and eat only vegetarian food.
Calorie-dense food packs a lot of energy into a small amount of food, so it helps you gain weight. Ghee and whey shakes are examples.
Whey is a protein found in milk. It is sold as a powder that people mix into shakes to build muscle.
Ghee is butter that has been cooked until the water and milk solids are removed. It is used a lot in Indian cooking.
To be transformed is to be changed completely, like a caterpillar turning into a butterfly.
A warrior is a person who fights bravely, especially in battle. Here the wrestler uses the word to describe his deepest nature.
An army brat is a child of a soldier. These families move often to new bases, so the kids keep changing schools.
A medallist is someone who has won a medal in a competition. An amateur is someone who competes without being paid.
Body positivity is the idea that people of every size and shape should feel good about their bodies.
Thanksgiving is an American holiday in late November when families eat a big meal, often turkey. Sushi would be a surprise guest there.
To Americanise something is to change it so that it fits American tastes and habits.
Combative means ready and eager to fight or argue.
Ceremonial means part of a formal ritual or ceremony, done for tradition rather than for any practical need.
Authentic means real and true to the original, not a copy.
Compression shorts are tight, stretchy shorts that hug the body. Athletes wear them for support or under other clothes.
To sneak something is to do it quietly so that no one notices. Here wrestlers might slip shorts underneath the mawashi.
To swoon originally meant to faint from strong feeling. Today it means to be so charmed by something that you fall in love with it.
